plan.title: UC inflamed vs control: GSVA hallmark pathway scores + heatmap
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 12 colon samples (6 UC-inflamed vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch), raw Salmon gene-level counts for 12000 genes, with sample_01 flagged at ~4x below median library size. To answer 'a pathway activity score for every sample, and a heatmap of hallmark activity separating treated from control', the plan first runs sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) so the low-depth sample is inspected rather than silently dropped, then a standard DESeq2 differential expression pass (minimal pre-filter, median-of-ratios normalization, Wald test with apeglm shrinkage, BH-adjusted results) to establish the gene-level baseline and give a ranked statistic. The core deliverable is GSVA: per-sample enrichment scores for the 50 MSigDB Hallmark gene sets computed directly on the normalized/VST expression matrix (Poisson kernel appropriate for count-derived data), giving one score per sample per pathway as requested. Those 50 x 12 GSVA scores are then tested with limma using the same UC-inflamed vs control design to identify which hallmark pathways significantly separate the two groups, and visualized as a clustered heatmap (samples x hallmark pathways, annotated by condition and by the flagged low-depth sample) so the separating pathways are visible directly. A brief report step consolidates thresholds, versions, and the low-depth-sample caveat.

steps.method: vst(blind) PCA + sample distance heatmap + library size QC

GSVA per-sample pathway scores (Poisson kernel on counts) on MSigDB Hallmark, then limma on scores for group comparison, plus heatmap
pathway score heatmap + limma results summary
